$schema_description: Curriculum Categorization Template: Sections and Question Topics. Use this template to categorize all course content and patterns discovered across past exams into coherent syllabus sections with exactly 2 to 4 question topics per section. This file defines the master topic taxonomy used to tag questions.

markdown_and_latex_support.note: Textual fields support Markdown and LaTeX math ($math$).
markdown_and_latex_support.mandatory_json_backslash_rule: In JSON strings, every LaTeX backslash MUST be double-escaped as \\ (e.g. '$O(1)$', '$\alpha$'). Single backslashes like \t or \f corrupt text or crash JSON parsers.

course.title: EXPLANATION: Full official course name (e.g. 'Internet Architecture and Protocols')
course.subtitle: EXPLANATION: Key thematic focus areas of the course (e.g. 'Advanced Transport Protocols, Congestion Control & Web Evolution')
course.description: EXPLANATION: 1-2 sentence overview of the course scope and syllabus categorization.

sections.number: EXPLANATION: Section or module number string (e.g. '1', '2', 'Module I')
sections.title: EXPLANATION: Descriptive section title covering a broad course theme (e.g. 'Internet Architecture & End-to-End Design Principles')
sections.subtitle: EXPLANATION: 1-line conceptual subtitle summarizing this section's focus (e.g. 'Fate-Sharing, Soft State, Heterogeneity & The End-to-End Argument')
sections.summary: EXPLANATION: 1-2 sentence overview explaining the central problems, architecture, or mechanisms covered in this section.
sections.badge: EXPLANATION: Visual category badge label (e.g. 'Foundations', 'High Frequency', 'Advanced Architecture', 'Core Protocols')

topics.id: EXPLANATION: Unique topic ID string matching what will be referenced in questions (e.g. 'topic-1-1', 'topic-fate-sharing')
topics.title: EXPLANATION: Specific question topic title (e.g. 'Fate-Sharing & State Placement in Intermediate Nodes')
topics.summary: EXPLANATION: 1-2 sentence crisp definition of the specific technical concepts, tradeoffs, or protocols assessed under this topic.
topics.badge: EXPLANATION: Optional topic priority or style badge (e.g. 'Exam Core', 'Recurring Conceptual', 'Analytical / Calculation')

topics.id: EXPLANATION: Unique topic ID for second topic in section (e.g. 'topic-1-2', 'topic-soft-state')
topics.title: EXPLANATION: Second question topic title within this section (e.g. 'Soft State vs. Hard State & Survivability')
topics.summary: EXPLANATION: 1-2 sentence summary of this topic's technical scope and core trade-offs.

sections.title: Example Real Section: Active Queue Management (AQM) & Bufferbloat
sections.subtitle: Queue Delay Tracking, Sojourn Times, Dropping vs Marking & CoDel/FQ-CoDel Mechanics
sections.summary: Mechanisms designed to control standing queue delay at network bottlenecks without sacrificing high link utilization.

topics.title: Bufferbloat & AQM Design Principles
topics.summary: Distinguishing standing queues from transient bursts, and why oversized unmanaged drop-tail buffers inflate RTT.

topics.title: CoDel & Sojourn Time Control (Target & Interval)
topics.summary: Tracking minimum packet packet delay over a sliding 100 ms interval against a 5 ms target threshold.

topics.title: Flow Queueing CoDel (FQ-CoDel) & Flow Isolation
topics.summary: Combining fair flow queueing hash buckets with CoDel AQM to isolate latency-sensitive flows from bulk senders.
